title: FlatCAM Plus main window — restyle directions
brief: Three visual directions for restyling the existing FlatCAM Plus main window (object tree, notebook tabs, plot canvas, tool parameters), built on the color tokens that flatcam_plus/appGUI/PanelStyles.py and appGUI/themes/*_style_sheet.py actually ship.

artboards.title: Dense CAD dark
artboards.tradeoff: Keeps the shipped dark palette and the shipped three-dock layout, tightened: 24px tree rows, per-object kind column, orange focus and active state, always-on console. Maximum information per pixel and no relearning for existing users, but brutal for a newcomer and it inherits the app's weak light-theme focus behaviour in reverse (orange focus is strong, everything else competes with it).

artboards.title: Light workbench with inspector
artboards.tradeoff: Restructures around the job instead of the widgets: objects grouped by stage (Imported / Generated / Machining), a five-step job stepper, and one selection-driven inspector that replaces three separate tool-tab docks. Far clearer hierarchy and no lost settings, but it concedes persistent canvas width, hides inactive tool parameters behind selection, and adopts the vendor #0081db accent as the single light accent — a decision, since the shipped panel dict uses #b9d1ff.

artboards.title: Canvas-first with command palette
artboards.tradeoff: Collapses chrome to a labeled 72px rail plus a floating context toolbar and a bottom object strip, freeing most of the window for the plot, with a Ctrl+K palette for tool and object access. Best canvas-per-screen and fastest for keyboard users, but weakest discoverability of the tool set: the labeled rail is load-bearing for accessibility here, and the palette must stay a shortcut rather than the only route to any action.
